text:
samir (support): heads up — customer (+cassandra) seeing repeated 5xx from hosted inference since 12:03 UTC. lots of gateway 502/503. they say retries get 504s. sample request id: req_3f9b7d2a. stack traces attached (below).

jess (oncall): copying in eng-runtime and eng-platform. can you paste a full curl and correlation id? any spike in latency? :eyes:

cassandra (customer): here's a sample curl and response — we hit this on every request for ~10m then it started partially recovering.
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_***" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< x-request-id: req_3f9b7d2a
< content-type: application/json
{ "error": { "message": "upstream service error: routing-policy timeout", "code": 502 } }
```

samir (support): we also got a bunch of errors in proxylb logs referencing controlplane auth timeouts + config DB read timeouts. capturing a tail of the proxy logs: 
```
[2026-03-14T12:02:59Z] INFO request=req_3f9b7d2a route=generate -> controlplane/routing lookup
[2026-03-14T12:03:00Z] WARN controlplane call=authservice timeout=15000ms err="context deadline exceeded"
[2026-03-14T12:03:01Z] ERROR controlplane call=configdb read timeout=12000ms err="timeout"
[2026-03-14T12:03:01Z] ERROR upstream=runtime return_code=502 message="dependency failure"
```

jess (oncall): ok — sounds like control-plane dependency cascade: auth/session or routing-policy hitting config DB. @mike can you check routing-policy service metrics and DB connection pool? any recent deploys?

mike (eng-runtime): i'm seeing a sharp increase in p99 latency for /routing/resolve around 12:02. connection pool exhaustion to configdb (max connections reached) then timeouts. no runtime deploy at that time. looks like a sudden fanout from controlplane — maybe a misbehaving backfill job or a spike in feature rollout evaluations.

zoe (eng-platform): i can confirm a configdb scaling event earlier — controlplane jobs triggered a heavy migration at 11:58 and autoscaler didn't bring enough read replicas online quickly. scaling caught up at ~12:10 which explains partial recovery.

jess (oncall): good sleuthing. mitigation options while scaling finishes: 1) temporarily enable routing-policy cached fallback so requests don't synchronously hit configdb, 2) fail open auth for existing sessions (less safe), or 3) route to Dedicated fallback pool (if customer has dedicated). what's lowest-risk?

mike (eng-runtime): prefer cached fallback for routing-policy — config has TTLs and should reduce qps to configdb. i'll prepare a fast rollback toggle. adding circuit-break to short-circuit failed lookups to default routing.

samir (support): told customer we're investigating and applying fallback. asked them to hold traffic for 10m if they prefer no degraded results. they're okay with degraded fallback for immediate relief. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: roll started by mike — feature-toggle routing.cached_fallback=true for controlplane namespace

mike (eng-runtime): flip done. edge caches warmed; observing drop in configdb qps and routing-policy p99 latency down ~80% within 40s. proxylb 502s dropping.

cassandra (customer): confirming our integration is back to normal, we're getting 200s again. thanks for fast turnaround.

jess (oncall): root cause notes for postmortem: controlplane migration/mass backfill caused spike in configdb connections => connection pool exhaustion => routing-policy timeouts => auth/session calls slowed => upstream 502/503/504 returned to hosted inference API. immediate mitigation = enable routing-policy cached fallback. medium-term fixes = increase configdb read replica autoscale headroom, add queueing/throttling for backfill jobs, instrument per-job QPS limits.

samir (support): opened ticket SUP-2026-218 linking logs and customer convo. tagging eng-runtime + eng-platform for postmortem and runbook updates.

mike (eng-runtime): i'll add a short-term knob to default fallback TTL and a dashboard for controlplane->configdb connection queue length. also propose increasing connection pool with connection multiplexing for routing-policy clients.

zoe (eng-platform): i'll change autoscaling thresholds and add pre-warm policies for large migrations. also will add an alert: sustained configdb max-conns > 80% for >1m.

jess (oncall): leaving this thread open for final postmortem link. thanks everyone. :rocket:
